goalInfo.label: Investigate a specific hazard
goalInfo.detail: Full screening: Astroflare asks about the environment, the equipment and the safeguards, then reports conditions that warrant review.

steps.title: The problem
steps.purpose: Pick the hazard to investigate. This decides which questions come next.

questions.label: Hazard under investigation
questions.ask: Which hazard do you want to investigate?
questions.why: The applicable rules and inputs depend on the hazard.
questions.help: A what-if hazard pathway, not a prediction that it will occur.

questions.label: Research question (optional)
questions.ask: What do you most need to find out? (optional)
questions.why: Shown at the top of the report. Astroflare screens conditions; it cannot answer questions about probability or acceptability.
questions.help: Shown with the results. Astroflare screens a fixed set of conditions; it cannot answer questions about probability or acceptability.
questions.placeholder: Leave blank to use the default screening question

steps.title: Cabin environment
steps.purpose: Gravity, oxygen and pressure are the three inputs the screening cannot run without.

questions.label: Gravity
questions.ask: What gravity regime does this apply to?
questions.why: Gravity changes flame and smoke behaviour, and the data that apply.

questions.label: Oxygen fraction
questions.ask: What is the cabin oxygen fraction?
questions.why: Oxygen content strongly affects material flammability; it is also needed to compute oxygen partial pressure.
questions.help: Percent by volume of the cabin atmosphere.

questions.label: Total cabin pressure
questions.ask: What is the total cabin pressure?
questions.why: Needed for oxygen partial pressure and to decide which test data apply.

steps.title: Mission context
steps.purpose: Context for the report and for how much outside help the crew can count on.

questions.label: Habitat or vehicle
questions.ask: What kind of vehicle or habitat is it?
questions.why: Context for the report.

questions.label: Mission phase
questions.ask: Which mission phase are you looking at?
questions.why: Whether a crew is present to respond changes what can be assumed.

questions.label: Mission duration
questions.ask: How long is the mission (or the interval you care about), in days?
questions.why: Context; the cited literature lists extended duration among factors beyond past experience but gives no threshold.

questions.label: Crew size
questions.ask: How many crew are aboard?
questions.why: Context for response capacity and exposure.

questions.label: Return or safe-haven options
questions.ask: If something went wrong, what return or safe-haven options exist?
questions.why: Limits how much of the response can rely on outside help.

options.label: Quick return or safe haven available
No quick return / far from resupply

questions.label: One-way communication delay to ground
questions.ask: What is the one-way communication delay to ground, in minutes?
questions.why: Sets the shortest possible time for a ground reply.

steps.title: The circuit
steps.purpose: Voltage and current give the circuit's nominal power; the equipment type frames the fault behaviour.

questions.label: Equipment type
questions.ask: What kind of electrical equipment is involved?
questions.why: Different equipment has different fault and heating behaviour.

questions.label: Operating voltage
questions.ask: What is the operating voltage of the circuit, in volts?
questions.why: With operating current gives the circuit's nominal power.

questions.label: Operating current
questions.ask: What current does the circuit normally carry, in amperes?
questions.why: With operating voltage gives the circuit's nominal power.

steps.title: Faults and protection
steps.purpose: Fault current and clearing time give the let-through energy (I²t). Protection is a proposed mitigation until it is tested.

questions.label: Prospective fault current
questions.ask: What is the prospective fault current, in amperes?
questions.why: With the clearing time gives the let-through energy (I²t), the quantity used in the cited ignition-test methodology.

questions.label: Fault clearing time of the protective device
questions.ask: How long does the protective device take to clear a fault, in milliseconds?
questions.why: With the fault current gives the let-through energy (I²t).

questions.label: Fault protection
questions.ask: What fault protection does this circuit have?
questions.why: A specified protection is a proposed mitigation; a tested one is evidence.

options.label: Protective devices specified and tested for this circuit

questions.label: Procedure to remove power from the affected equipment
questions.ask: Is there a procedure to remove power from the affected equipment?
questions.why: The ISS response sequence in the cited brief includes removing electrical power to cease continuous ignition sources.

questions.label: Redundancy and emergency power
questions.ask: What happens to other loads if this circuit is de-energised? Is there redundancy or emergency power?
questions.why: Determines what is lost when the circuit is de-energised.

options.label: Redundant power paths and emergency power defined

questions.label: Inspection and maintenance history
questions.ask: Is the inspection and maintenance history of this equipment documented?
questions.why: Condition of wiring and connections cannot be assessed without it.

steps.title: Airflow
steps.purpose: Ventilation can feed a flame and spread smoke, but detectors depend on it. These answers give the air-turnover time scale.

questions.label: Volume of the affected compartment
questions.ask: What is the volume of the affected compartment, in m³?
questions.why: With the ventilation flow it gives the air turnover time scale.

questions.label: Ventilation flow through the compartment
questions.ask: What ventilation flow passes through that compartment, in m³/min?
questions.why: With the compartment volume it gives the air turnover time scale.

questions.label: Ability to stop ventilation to the affected compartment
questions.ask: Can ventilation to that compartment be stopped?
questions.why: Airflow can supply a fire with air and spread smoke, but detectors rely on airflow; the trade-off depends on this.

steps.title: Detection, suppression and response
steps.purpose: What would notice a fire, what could stop it, and who could respond.

questions.label: Fire detection coverage
questions.ask: How much of the compartment do fire detectors cover?
questions.why: Time to detection depends on where detectors are.

questions.label: Fire signatures detected
questions.ask: Which fire signatures can the detectors sense?
questions.why: Fire emissions depend on the fuel, heating conditions, gravity and atmosphere.

questions.label: Fire suppression provisions
questions.ask: What suppression provisions are available?
questions.why: Provisions differ in what they can reach and what they require of the crew.

options.label: Fixed or installed system plus portable, access verified

questions.label: Crew breathing protection
questions.ask: Is crew breathing protection available and reachable?
questions.why: Combustion products can be immediately harmful at small concentrations.

questions.label: Crew fire-response practice
questions.ask: How current is crew fire-response practice?
questions.why: Response depends on practised procedures.

questions.label: Post-fire monitoring and clean-up
questions.ask: Is there a plan for monitoring and clean-up after a fire?
questions.why: Combustion products can remain after flames are out.

steps.title: Materials and other ignition sources
steps.purpose: Flammability data apply only to the conditions in which they were gathered.

questions.label: Material flammability evidence
questions.ask: What flammability test evidence exists for the materials in this compartment?
questions.why: Flammability data apply only to the conditions tested.

options.label: Tested for this atmosphere and gravity

questions.label: Other ignition sources considered
questions.ask: What other ignition sources have been considered?
questions.why: Used by the heuristic screening index.
